fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders locate the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the single driveway entrance clearly so responding units can identify it without delay on approach.
• Keep the primary walkway clear of planters, furniture, or landscaping growth that could slow responder movement to the front door.
• Trim vegetation along the driveway and walkway edges so responders can move without obstruction.
• Cut back dense vegetation near the detached structure so responders can reach and work around it.
• Install a reflective marker or sign at the rear of the property to help responders locate the detached structure from the access point.
• Keep a clear path between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move between buildings without navigating around overgrown landscaping.
• If a gate provides rear access, keep it unlocked or secured with a standardized lock box so responders are not blocked.
• Mark any gate or secondary access point with a visible sign so responders do not waste time searching for entry along the perimeter fencing.
• Identify and communicate the single access point to your local fire department so they can note it in pre-arrival planning records.
• Keep the patio area and surrounding open space clear of large furniture or stored items that could block responder staging near the residence.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin the tree clusters nearest to the structure to create more open space between the trees and the building.
• Remove or trim shrubs that are growing directly against or within a few feet of the structure.
• Separate the scattered shrubs from nearby vegetation groups to reduce connected patches of plants that could carry fire toward the structure.
• Trim lower branches on scattered trees near the structure to raise the canopy off the ground.
• Keep vegetation groups near the structure thinned so fire cannot move easily from one group to the next toward the building.
• Maintain the open green space by keeping grass mowed short, especially where it connects to shrubs or tree clusters near the structure.
• Keep all access routes clear of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation so vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Trim branches that overhang or lean toward the roofline from nearby trees.
